title: Affine torsion comparison for a Cartier-factor blow-up chart
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $I\subseteq A$ be an ideal, let $a\in I$, let $x\in A$ be a nonzerodivisor, and let $M$ be an $A$-module with $\Gamma_{(x)}(M)=0$. Put $B=A[I/a]$, the affine blow-up chart algebra [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring], and regard $a$ and $xa$ as elements of $B$ through $A\to B$. Then the power-torsion submodules agree:

$$\Gamma_{(a)}(M\otimes_A B)=\Gamma_{(xa)}(M\otimes_A B).$$

Here $\Gamma_{(r)}$ is the submodule of elements killed by some positive power of $r$ [def-nagata-power-torsion].

source.place: Tag 080H, proof of lemma-strict-transform-different-centers, algebra reduction paragraph (the assertion that a-power torsion equals xa-power torsion in M tensor A[I/a]).

proof.text: Set $S=\{1,a,a^2,\ldots\}$, $L=A_a$ and $N=M\otimes_A B$. By [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring], $B$ is an $A$-subalgebra of $L$, so its inclusion $i:B\to L$ is injective. It is a localization of the $A$-module $B$ at $S$, in the explicit sense of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-product]: (a) every $a^n$ acts bijectively on $L$, since $a$ is invertible there; (b) every element of $L$ is $c/a^r$ with $c\in A$, and hence is $a^{-r}i(\overline c)$ for the structural image $\overline c\in B$; (c) $i(b)=i(b')$ implies $b=b'$ by the subalgebra inclusion, so the equality criterion holds with $s=1$. The ring map $A\to L$ is a localization at $S$ by [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. These statements also hold when $a$ is nilpotent and $L=B=0$.

source.place: Tag 080H, lemma-strict-transform-different-centers, proof of (2), affine algebra paragraph.

proof.text: Take the module localization $\lambda:M\to M_a$, $m\mapsto m/1$, of [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-product] with base ring $A$, localization algebra $L$, module pair $(M,B)$, localized pair $(M_a,L)$ and maps $(\lambda,i)$; Step 1 checks the second map's hypotheses. It says that $N\to M_a\otimes_L L$, $m\otimes b\mapsto(m/1)\otimes i(b)$, is a localization at $S$. The balanced map $M_a\otimes_L L\to M_a$, $v\otimes t\mapsto tv$, has inverse $v\mapsto v\otimes1$: the two compositions are the identity because $tv\otimes1=v\otimes t$ and pure tensors generate [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Thus the composite $j:N\to M_a$, $j(m\otimes b)=i(b)(m/1)$, has the same localization properties (a)--(c). Define $u:M\to N$ by $u(m)=m\otimes1$, using the same tensor universal property. The formula gives $ju=\lambda$.

source.place: Tag 080H, lemma-strict-transform-different-centers, proof of (2), affine algebra paragraph.

proof.text: We spell out the kernel and cokernel assertion about $u$ in Tag 080H. If $u(m)=0$, then $m/1=ju(m)=0$; the fraction criterion in [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away] gives $a^s m=0$ for some $s\geq0$. For $z\in N$, write $j(z)=m/a^r$ in $M_a$. Then $j(a^r z-u(m))=0$. Property (c) of the localization $j$ in Step 2, as stated in [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-product], gives $a^k(a^r z-u(m))=0$ for some $k\geq0$. Consequently $a^{k+r}z=u(a^km)$. Hence every element of $\ker u$ is killed by a power of $a$, and every element of $N$ has a power-of-$a$ multiple in $\operatorname{im}u$.

source.place: Tag 080H, lemma-strict-transform-different-centers, proof of (2), affine algebra paragraph.

proof.text: If $z\in\Gamma_{(xa)}(N)$, choose $n\geq1$ with $(xa)^nz=0$ [def-nagata-power-torsion]. By Step 3 choose $r\geq0$ and $m\in M$ with $a^rz=u(m)$. Then $u(x^na^nm)=x^na^{n+r}z=a^r(xa)^nz=0$. The kernel assertion of Step 3 gives $s\geq0$ such that $a^sx^na^nm=0$. Commutativity rewrites this as $x^n(a^{s+n}m)=0$. Since $\Gamma_{(x)}(M)=0$, its definition [def-nagata-power-torsion] gives $a^{s+n}m=0$. Therefore $a^{s+n+r}z=u(a^{s+n}m)=0$, proving $z\in\Gamma_{(a)}(N)$. Conversely, if $a^qz=0$ for some $q\geq1$, then $(xa)^qz=x^qa^qz=0$. The two submodules consequently have the same elements. The definition permits exponent zero; replacing a zero exponent by one gives the positive-exponent convention of the statement without changing either submodule.

source.place: Tag 080H, lemma-strict-transform-different-centers, proof of (2), affine algebra paragraph.
